<subject>Fw: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes</subject>
<body>
Sara,

Below is the memo I sent out September 19th summarizing the September 17th meeting. See second bullet item in my summary. I remember Manuella couldn't attend that day, but Marcelo was very active in discussions throughout the meeting. 

I couldn't find the copy I sent. Fortunately, Matteo still had his copy.
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From: Mendes, Matteo
Sent: Monday, December 16, 2024 10:20 AM
To: Ferreira, Heitor
Subject: FW: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes

FYI

-----Original Message-----
From: Ferreira, Heitor
Sent: Thursday, September 19, 2024 2:25 PM
To: Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc: Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject: Results of Meeting on Fleet Hub Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

Ribeirão Preto in 3 TransCarga by hub
The decision was made to sub-divide the Regional Distribution storage group into two zones; Ribeirão Preto and North of Sorocaba, rather than 3 zones or allocating by hub. If it is determined that additional divisions are necessary in the future, such changes can be made at that time. Changes to SIGMA are required. I have discussed the changes with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha and have learned that the changes are not difficult to make and could be made in a couple days.

Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will determine which deferred delivery points are in these new field regions and then provide the information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should this change be implemented immediately or should it wait until the beginning of the peak season?

Change from 'zero-buffer' approach / Provide minimum level of activity
The decision was made to table this concern for now. The scheduled activity that drives the allocation process does not guarantee physical route operations. In most cases, the flexibility provided by the network allows Logistics Control to adjust operations to maintain the required minimum level of shipments into Santos and Guarulhos. Further analysis is required. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will continue to monitor the system conditions/operations that effect physical capacity to determine if and what additional changes maybe warranted.

Send "Alert" when final scheduled volume exceeds operational capacity
The IT group will modify the scheduling cycle to add a procedure where the final net scheduled volume is compared to the operational capacity set for distribution. If the final scheduled volume exceeds operational capacity, I will receive a notification via e-mail. The purpose here is to monitor occurrences to determine the magnitude of the problem. I will get with Matteo Mendes to finalize the matter.
</quoted>
